question:
Each new version of our web service is switched on for every user at the same moment, so a single faulty version breaks the service for everyone and getting the previous version back takes hours. How should we change the way new versions go live to limit the damage?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
[JEV filter] kept 10 of 10 guidelines (JEV 'lenient' score > 0.5)

# Guidelines
- Adopt environment-based release strategies that use a staging environment before releasing to production. Deploy the new version first to a staging environment so issues are caught before all users are affected. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Release Engineering Strategies and Risk Reduction.md) [JEV 0.92]
- Use application-based release strategies with feature toggles (feature flags). These [SWEBOK excerpt 244b851be785515d6e01] [SWEBOK excerpt d8eaaf95a43c1559b4fb], so a faulty feature can be switched off instantly without redeploying. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Release Engineering Strategies and Risk Reduction.md) [JEV 0.92]
- Adopt canary release testing: perform [SWEBOK excerpt 4906aab7643dc67a4dea] evaluate that change before proceeding with a complete deployment. This limits the blast radius to only the users receiving the canary slice. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Automated Deployment and Canary Release Testing.md; root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Installation and Operational Verification Processes/Production Environment Testing and Verification/Production System Testing Challenges and Techniques.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Automate deployment surveillance so that newly started software is observed for a period after installation, and changes that do not pass the validation period are automatically rolled back — ideally so quickly that end users do not notice a problem. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Automated Deployment and Canary Release Testing.md; root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Rollback and Data Migration in Software Deployment.md; root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Rollback and Problem Resolution in DevOps.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Plan, design, and rehearse rollback and data migration before deploying any new version. Software engineers must ensure that both the software and its database can be quickly returned to a known-good state; a rollback strategy should be part of every change management assessment. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Rollback and Problem Resolution in DevOps.md; root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Rollback and Data Migration in Software Deployment.md; root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Engineering Operations Control Techniques.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Move to small, independent deployments rather than large bundled releases. [SWEBOK excerpt 65fed9f0efeec630a1f1] defect fix) on demand and independently, requiring the application to be architected accordingly. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/DevOps Continuous Delivery and Independent Deployments.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Implement product telemetry across all layers (application, OS, infrastructure) with analytics to detect problems as early as possible after a release, enabling prompt incident response before minor issues escalate. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Product Telemetry for Early Problem Detection.md; root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Monitor, Measure, Track, and Review.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Implement formal change management so that every change is assessed for risk and assigned a rollback strategy before it is approved. Changes should be classified (e.g., emergency, urgent, major, minor) and large changes scheduled with the product manager and end users. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Engineering Operations Control Techniques.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Automate the creation and synchronisation of all environments from a single source of truth (Infrastructure as Code), so that the staging and other pre-production environments accurately mirror production and validate releases before they go live. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Automated Environment Creation and Infrastructure as Code.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Conduct incident post-mortems after every significant production failure. Proper analysis of the cause of incidents [SWEBOK excerpt c53ea53da933f2d8f0d3] from occurring in the future. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Engineering Operations Control Techniques.md; root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Rollback and Problem Resolution in DevOps.md) [JEV 0.95]
